findings.citation: P. Berglund, T. Hübsch, D. Minić, "Dark energy and quantum gravity" (arXiv title "On Dark Energy and Quantum Gravity"), Int. J. Mod. Phys. D 28 (2019) 1944018, arXiv:1905.09463 (journal; Gravity Research Foundation essay)
findings.summary: In the doubled, non-commutative (metastring, Born-geometric) phase-space formulation of string theory, the dual coordinates x̃, the difference of left- and right-movers, span what the authors call 'the canonically conjugate dual space'. Integrating the doubled action −∫√−g(x)√−g̃(x̃)[R(x) + R̃(x̃)] (Tseytlin's form) over x̃ makes the size of the dual space set Newton's constant, and its curvature set a positive cosmological constant in the observed spacetime: the dual space's curvature 'provides for the dark energy'. The paper argues that non-commutativity stabilizes Λ, through the Grosse–Wulkenhaar solvability of non-commutative Φ⁴. It makes the same claim as the authors' Phys. Lett. B 798 (2019) 134950 (arXiv:1905.08269), which the C5 search group labeled partial. The record already quotes the same claim from BHM 2023 (arXiv:2212.06086) in papers/phase-space-diameter.md §4, for the self-dual length, and does not compare it with C5.
findings.difference: The attribution is static. Our Λ is the x̃-integrated curvature term of the dual space, not the contents of a contracting conjugate universe. Nothing contracts or collapses, and there is no a·ã = 1 dynamics, no dual-frame fluid and no w_eff = −w̃ dictionary. The two treatments assign the dual Einstein–Hilbert term differently: here it gives Λ, while #11 §10 makes the dual Einstein term an a⁻⁶ step in G_eff and maps dual curvature to negative dark radiation. That step is itself not derived (flag 49), and BHM's x̃-integration bears on it. BHM's dual space is the metastring's T-dual x̃ space, canonically conjugate to x; it is not the momentum-space description of one state selected by a spontaneously broken polarization.

Essentially, the curvature of the dual space is the cosmological constant in the observed spacetime, and the size of the dual space is the gravitational constant in the same observed spacetime.

findings.citation: P. Berglund, T. Hübsch, D. Minić, "On Stringy de Sitter Spacetimes", JHEP 12 (2019) 166, arXiv:1902.08617 (journal)
findings.summary: The paper's main content is a family of 3+1-dimensional de Sitter solutions in F-theory with an anisotropic axion-dilaton background. Its synopsis proposes that integrating over the 'dual/"momentum" string degrees of freedom' of the phase-space (metastring) formulation will naturally produce an effective de Sitter background, through an induced anisotropic dilaton profile whose anisotropy carries the positive cosmological constant. The authors present this as a proposal with 'some evidence ... but not a detailed proof'. It is the earliest of the three 2019 Berglund–Hübsch–Minić statements that our positive Λ comes from the dual sector (arXiv, February 2019).
findings.difference: It is a proposal, not a derivation, and it is static: the positive Λ comes from integrating out dual degrees of freedom, not from a contracting or collapsing conjugate universe. There is no a·ã = 1, no dual-frame fluid and no w_eff = −w̃. The de Sitter of the paper's actual solution comes from an anisotropic axion-dilaton profile in F-theory.

quotes.text: In that formulation, we can integrate over such dual/“momentum” string degrees of freedom in order to generate an effective spacetime description.
quotes.where: full text, section 1 (Introduction, Results and Synopsis), 'The Main Point'

quotes.text: Our proposal (for which we have some evidence from our solution, but not a detailed proof, as discussed in what follows) is that this procedure will naturally lead to an effective de Sitter background

findings.citation: P. Berglund, L. Freidel, T. Hübsch, J. Kowalski-Glikman, R. G. Leigh, D. Mattingly, D. Minic, "Infrared Properties of Quantum Gravity: UV/IR Mixing, Gravitizing the Quantum -- Theory and Observation", arXiv:2202.06890 (2022); Snowmass 2021 contribution, arXiv preprint only
findings.summary: This white paper restates the Berglund–Hübsch–Minić claim in one sentence, citing BHM 2019 (Phys. Lett. B 798 134950; Int. J. Mod. Phys. D 28 1944018). To leading order in the minimal length one gets a dual geometry, 'which in the observed spacetime leads to "dark energy", modeled as a positive cosmological constant'. Its co-authors include Freidel, Leigh and Kowalski-Glikman. The dark-matter reader records its C1 clause (each observed field's dual as dark matter) separately.
findings.difference: It is a citation summary of BHM 2019 and adds nothing new for C5. The same differences apply: a static dual geometry gives a positive Λ, with no contraction, collapse, a·ã = 1 or w_eff = −w̃.

quotes.text: Similarly, in the gravitational setting one gets, to leading order in the minimal length, a dual geometry, which in the observed spacetime leads to “dark energy”, modeled as a positive cosmological constant

findings.citation: L. Freidel, J. Kowalski-Glikman, R. G. Leigh, D. Minic, "Vacuum energy density and gravitational entropy", Phys. Rev. D 107 (2023) 126016, arXiv:2212.00901 (2022) (journal)
findings.summary: The paper rewrites the regularized vacuum energy as a sum over elementary phase-space cells (modular regularization). It bounds the vacuum energy density by the size of the regulated momentum space, which UV/IR mixing at fixed cell number N ties inversely to the size of spacetime. Equating N with the entropy of the de Sitter horizon gives ρ ≲ ħ/(ℓ²ℓ_P²), consistent with the observed value: 'the smallness of the vacuum energy is tied to the large size of the Universe'. The record cites this paper and the companion essay in papers/phase-space-diameter.md §4, for the self-dual length and the inverse relation of the cutoffs, not for C5.
findings.difference: This is a counting argument for the size of a constant vacuum energy, not a dynamical source of acceleration. Its 'momentum space' is the momentum range of vacuum fluctuations (the cutoff), not a conjugate description of the universe with its own scale factor and contents. Nothing contracts or collapses, and there is no dual-frame fluid and no w_eff = −w̃. The only shared theme is that dark energy is set on the momentum-space side, and that this side is small because the universe is large. The C5 search group read FKGLM 2022/2023 and judged them not relevant to C5; this reader records them as related, with low confidence.

quotes.text: Essentially, the smallness of the vacuum energy is tied to the large size of the Universe.
Heuristically one can say that the holographic bound on entropy precludes the size of momentum space (and thus effectively its cutoff) being as large as EFT assumes.
Having tied the vacuum energy density to the size of the cosmological horizon, this problem may be resolved as well.

findings.citation: L. Freidel, J. Kowalski-Glikman, R. G. Leigh, D. Minic, "On the inevitable lightness of vacuum", Int. J. Mod. Phys. D 32 (2023) 2342004, arXiv:2303.17495 (journal; essay)
findings.summary: This is the essay version of FKGLM 2022, and the record already cites it with that paper (papers/phase-space-diameter.md §4). The regularized vacuum energy density scales as the volume of energy–momentum space. A UV–IR regularization combined with the holographic entropy bound makes the cosmological constant small 'because the universe is filled with a large number of degrees of freedom'.
findings.difference: The same as for FKGLM 2022: the size of a constant vacuum energy is fixed by counting phase-space cells. There is no conjugate universe, no contraction or collapse, and no dictionary.

quotes.text: It follows that the universe is large, and the cosmological constant is naturally small, because the universe is filled with a large number of degrees of freedom.
the regularized vacuum energy density scales as the volume of energy-momentum space

findings.citation: D. Minic, "The Vacuum Energy Problem in Quantum Gravity and the Masses of Elementary Particles", arXiv:2305.12593 (2023), conference talk (BASIC 2023); published as Bulg. J. Phys. 51 (2024) 060
findings.summary: The talk summarizes the FKGLM account: the vacuum energy density is the volume of energy–momentum space, bounded through the Bekenstein bound by 1/(l²l_P²), which gives the see-saw length √(l l_P). It also states that the modular cell can be rescaled as x → a x, p → a⁻¹ p, and that in the limit of large expansion a → ∞ 'the dual dimension shrinks to zero and one recovers the usual spacetime'. That is a kinematic analogue of founding supposition 6 (a·ã = 1), used here for the decoupling limit to ordinary spacetime.
findings.difference: The same as for FKGLM 2022. The shrinking dual dimension is a decoupling limit of the modular cell, not the contraction of a conjugate universe in time, and it is tied neither to the acceleration nor to dark energy.

findings.citation: C. Castro Perelman, "Born's Reciprocal Relativity theory, curved phase space, Finsler geometry and the cosmological constant", Annals Phys. 416 (2020) 168143, doi:10.1016/j.aop.2020.168143 (journal; not on arXiv)
findings.summary: The paper treats gravity on the curved phase space (the cotangent bundle, in Finsler geometry) of Born's reciprocal relativity. A scalar-gravity model has exact solutions in which the base spacetime and the internal momentum space are both (anti-)de Sitter, and the abstract says they 'capture the very early inflationary and very-late-time de Sitter phases'. Regularizing the 8-dimensional phase-space action gives a tiny effective cosmological constant, which the field equations correlate with a tiny four-dimensional Λ. Only the abstract was read. The paper is not on arXiv, its full text is paywalled, and WebSearch found no free copy.
findings.difference: The abstract alone shows the late-time de Sitter phase and the small Λ coming from solutions and a regularization of phase-space gravity. It indicates no contracting momentum-space universe acting on ours, no dual-frame fluid and no w_eff = −w̃. Momentum space is the fibre of the cotangent bundle with a fixed (A)dS curvature, not a conjugate description of the universe's state. The full text might qualify this.

quotes.text: The curved base spacetime manifold and internal momentum space both turn out to be (Anti) de Sitter type.
The most salient feature is that the solutions capture the very early inflationary and very-late-time de Sitter phases of the Universe.
A regularization of the 8-dim phase space action leads naturally to an extremely small effective cosmological constant

findings.citation: P. O. Hess, "Observable consequences of pseudo-complex General Relativity", arXiv:2101.04152 (2021), arXiv preprint (no journal found in INSPIRE or Crossref)
findings.summary: Pseudo-complex general relativity (pc-GR) starts from Born's point that quantum mechanics treats coordinates and momenta on an equal footing. It extends the coordinates to X = x + I y, with y_μ = A l u_μ, a minimal length times the four-velocity (the Born–Caianiello velocity-space part). In the pc-Robertson–Walker model (§4.5) the scale factor becomes a = a_R + I a_I, and to leading order a_I = l ȧ_R(0)/a_R⁴: the velocity-like partner shrinks as our scale factor grows ('it continues to be even smaller for larger times'). The paper ties the growth of a_I toward the Big Bang to 'a dominance of the dark energy' there. It obtains today's acceleration from a dark-energy density Λ a_R^{3(β−1)}, which for β = 1 is a cosmological constant.
findings.difference: The two elements of C5 appear in one model but are not linked as C5 links them. The shrinking partner a_I is not the source of the late acceleration, which comes from the dark-energy density Λ a_R^{3(β−1)} (constant for β = 1), and its influence runs the other way: large a_I goes with dark-energy dominance near the Big Bang. Its law is a_I ∝ a_R⁻⁴, not a·ã = 1, and there is no conjugate matter, no collapse and no w_eff = −w̃. The pseudo-imaginary part is velocity space in Caianiello's sense, not a spontaneously selected polarization.

findings.citation: G. Caspar, T. Schönenbach, P. O. Hess, M. Schäfer, W. Greiner, "Pseudo-Complex General Relativity: Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordström and Kerr Solutions", Int. J. Mod. Phys. E 21 (2012) 1250015, arXiv:1202.6561 (journal)
findings.summary: In pc-GR, a theory with Born–Caianiello-motivated pseudo-complex coordinates whose length element the paper says 'is equal to the one used by M. Born', the modified variational principle adds a term 'interpreted as dark energy'. That term accumulates around a central mass and halts gravitational collapse, so a 'gray star' forms instead of a black hole. Four other pc-GR papers on this reading list use the same wording: recid 1268217 (Int. J. Mod. Phys. D 19, 2010), 1303626 (2013 chapter), 1402205 (Springer Proc. Phys. 170, 2016), whose abstract reads 'a collapsing mass increasingly accumulates dark energy until the collapse is stopped', and 1487060 (PoS FFP14 036). A search for 'collapse', 'dark energy' and 'Born' meets them.
findings.difference: Only the words coincide. The collapse is ordinary stellar collapse in position space, and the dark energy resists it. Nothing concerns a conjugate universe or the cosmic acceleration.

quotes.text: It is shown, that the pc-GR introduces automatically terms into the system which can be interpreted as dark energy.
The energy accumulates around a central mass and halts the collapse of a big star.
is equal to the one used by M. Born and related theories

findings.citation: J. Govaerts, P. D. Jarvis, S. O. Morgan, S. G. Low, "World-line quantisation of a reciprocally invariant system", J. Phys. A 40 (2007) 12095, arXiv:0706.3736 (journal)
findings.summary: In Low's reciprocal relativity (quaplectic group), 'cosmological constant' is the world-line cosmological constant, the constant in the reparametrization constraint of a particle action. The constraint identifies it with a fixed value of the quaplectic Casimir. The sequel, Jarvis and Morgan, J. Phys. A 41 (2008) 465203 (arXiv:0806.4794, recid 789406, also on this list), uses the term the same way. A search for 'reciprocal relativity' with 'cosmological constant' meets both.
findings.difference: Only the words coincide. The world-line cosmological constant has nothing to do with the cosmic expansion, dark energy or a conjugate universe.

quotes.text: Imposition of the first class constraint, the generator of local time reparametrisations, on physical states enforces identification of the world-line cosmological constant with a fixed value of the quadratic Casimir of the quaplectic symmetry group

notes: 47 flagged papers, conjecture C5: 11 findings, 36 not relevant, 0 unavailable. No paper states C5. None has a conjugate (momentum-space or dual) universe whose contraction or collapse drives our accelerated expansion, and none uses a dual-frame fluid or a w_eff = −w̃ dictionary. The closest on this list is the Berglund–Hübsch–Minić line (1905.09463 partial, medium; 1902.08617 and the Snowmass restatement 2202.06890 partial, low): the x̃-integrated curvature of the 'canonically conjugate dual space' is our Λ. That is static, with no collapse, and it assigns the dual Einstein–Hilbert term differently from #11 §10, which bears on flag 49. The record already quotes BHM 2023's version of the claim (papers/phase-space-diameter.md §4, for the self-dual length) without comparing it with C5. Related, low: the FKGLM vacuum-energy line (2212.00901, 2303.17495, 2305.12593, recid 2778134; the C5 search group judged FKGLM not relevant, a deliberate disagreement); Castro Perelman 2020 (abstract only); Hess 2021 pc-Robertson–Walker model (velocity-like partner scale factor a_I ∝ a_R⁻⁴, not linked to the acceleration). Collisions: pc-GR 'collapse ... dark energy' (gray stars; one entry, 1202.6561, for the family of five) and the world-line 'cosmological constant' of reciprocal relativity (0706.3736; sequel 0806.4794). Method: lit.py show for all 47; lit.py text with three greps (dark energy/acceleration; contract|collaps|shrink; dual/conjugate/momentum-space universe terms) on the 38 arXiv ids, each cosmology hit read in context. PDFs: 2110.11343, 2211.04909 and PoS FFP14 036 fetched with WebFetch and read with a stdlib-only extractor, each in its own folder. The Maheshwari thesis was read from the r2 reader's extracted text. Abstract only: recid 1789711, 1402205, 1303626, 1268217, 870803, 2669772, 2778134. All 27 reported quotes FOUND by lit.py quote, and each finding passes recheck.py's identifier, title, author and year checks (scripts/recheck_out.py). Leads outside C5, not findings: Toller 2017 (1706.07470), a spontaneously broken 'augmented Lorentz covariance' (Born reciprocity its first example) with Goldstone fields proposed to replace dark energy and dark matter, a lead for the hard core and τ; Moffat 2004 (gr-qc/0401117), Einstein-type field equations for a momentum-space metric, a lead for founding supposition 10; Artigas, Crowe, Mielczarek 2020 (2003.08129), a compact phase space making a Λ universe recollapse, a follow-up to the closed-universe lead Artigas–Mielczarek–Rovelli 2019; 2202.06890's C1 clause, already recorded by the dark-matter reader. Notes, greps, extracted texts and the quote checks are in work/literature-check/round2/r3-dark-energy/.
